OC - Some shelves for the kitchen

Made some shelves to store food and kitchen stuff. Turned out pretty good,

https://files.catbox.moe/m9s6kx.jpg

Shelves are made from reclaimed hardwood floor boards, glued up and roughly planed on the top. I didn't bother planing the bottom other than where the shelves rest on the frame.

https://files.catbox.moe/d76idr.jpg

The frames were made from 1" square tube. It's a bit heavier than I probably needed, but I suck pretty bad at welding, so I got 2.5mm thick.

https://files.catbox.moe/efqbkb.jpg

Some of the shelves are (theoretically) adjustable, they are held up by brackets that are screwed into the main fraim with 1/4-20 screws. To make these, I made a quick jig that

was able to hold the flanges accurately and consistently in place while I tacked them.

https://files.catbox.moe/majnc7.jpg

To level the shelf I welded in some flanged M10

nuts to the bottom. The nuts were just a little too big to fit into a 15mm hole (which was the largest hole I could easily drill) so I popped them in the lathe and trimmed off the corners until

they fit. This allowed me to use some socket head M10 bolts, which I can use to adjust the height from above.

https://files.catbox.moe/bkz9lg.jpg

The bolts have a taper (about 20 degrees), this is to mate into some shallow holes drilled into some feet I made out of 25x5mm steel bar (I forgot to take a photo of them).

https://files.catbox.moe/twxgq2.jpg

All the bits were taken inside and assembled with some help.

https://files.catbox.moe/0u9290.jpg
I like it, and it looks good now, but I'd worry that the shelves would bow when put weight on it

They're actually very sturdy. The floor boards are 16-17mm thick and don't flex noticeably even if I'm standing on them. You'd have to put several hundred kilos on a shelf to get any flex out of them (would probably shear off the bolts on the adjustable shelf before flexing much). It'll be used for storing kitchen stuff mainly, so I don't expect each shelf section to have more than about 40kg on it.

https://files.catbox.moe/m9s6kx.jpgJPG

Here, the top shelf that's loaded with tomatoes has 36 bottles, each weigh about 750g, so that's 27kg. That's probably the most heavily loaded shelf so far.

Since it's solid wood, it's much sturdier than if it was something like MDF or particle board.

I hope you're right. Sometimes the bows occurs gradually over time, maybe changes in humidity and temperature have something to do with it. I had a tv stand once that didn't bend at all at first when I put a plasma tv on it but it bowed eventually.

I'm pretty confident that they'll hold up. Have a large bookshelf in the design phase at the moment that I'll be using a similar method although it will have wooden frames rather than steel, and some Kumiko details.

Since it's reclaimed flooring, it'll generally be less prone to warping or twisting as it's been acclimatized for a long time (could be 100 years old some of this stuff). There was generally a little cupping in each of the boards, but basically no twist or bow. The cupping was planed out where it was enough to raise a lip between the boards.
